changed_without_a_release.reading: release = row flag `fired` (x_release/out/release_change.json: ReScope-W, at any position); a row counts if fired is false and D1 is true.  If the flag were the last-position flag only, the rows without a release at any position would be a subset of the rows counted here, so 0 holds under either reading.  The gate rows (rescope, the cosine family, retr_sum) carry src = pre: the pre-edit outcome was assigned without a forward pass, 0 holds by construction there and is no measurement.

a.statement: Sec. 5.3: a release of ReScope changes the answer on every released held-out query; on near-scope negatives on at least 95 percent of the released
a.verdict: TRUE as printed: held-out, every released row has D1 set in each of the 3 draws on both development logs (and on all 13 logs); near-scope, smallest value 95.11 % as mean over the 3 draws (pooled over the draws 95.45 %; smallest single draw 93.10 %); in a single draw the share falls below 95 %: the statement holds for the mean over the draws, which is what the macro prints

b.statement: Sec. 5.4: release on held-out probes that ask an edit's question is 3 to 23 percent, and 0 to 9 of 20 calibration draws per log exceed the level
b.verdict: numbers TRUE over the 13 logs of the experiment (3.2 to 22.6 %; draws 0 to 9 of 20); SCOPE: the upper end 22.6 % is the DEVELOPMENT log TB-Q100-ae-l2_3; over the 11 unseen logs alone the release is 3.2 to 13.2 % (the draws range 0 to 9 is the same with or without the development logs).  The paragraph is about the unseen logs.

c.statement: report: H2 18 of 22 rejected, all against ReScope; H3 27 of 33, 25 against and 2 in favour
c.verdict: H2 TRUE and robust (18 of 22, 18 against, 0 in favour; the same with my own resamples).  H3 REPRODUCED (27 of 33, 25 against, 2 in favour, from the stored values and from my replication of the experiment's 2000 resamples) but NOT ROBUST: the member 'TB-Q100-memitw | PairOne' has stored p 0.005 (Holm 0.036); with 820000 own resamples p = 0.00703 +- 0.00013 against the rejection limit 0.05 / 7 = 0.00714, Holm-adjusted 0.0492; my first 20000 resamples gave Holm 0.0623, i.e. 26 of 33 (24 against, 2 in favour).  The 27th rejection depends on the Monte Carlo error of a 2000-resample value.

stored.family: the two differences to linear repairs on the two development logs (4 tests: backbones x the two choices of the best linear repair)
stored.note: a bootstrap p at 1 / n_boot means that no resample crossed 0: the Holm-adjusted value is then an upper bound
